history.summary: NON-HINDU (Jain) - KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED. Group of three surviving stone Jain temples (rekha deul in Pala architecture) in Pakbirra village, Puncha block, ~40-50 km southeast of Purulia town. Purulia was an important Jain centre from the 6th to 13th century. Documented in 1865 by C. J. Beavan (three temples standing); surveyed for ASI by J. D. Beglar, who recorded nearly two dozen temples, mostly Jain, and a colossal 7.5-ft standing Jina (identified by the lotus pedestal emblem). The colossal statue is now worshipped locally as Bhirabnath/Shiva - an unusual Hindu appropriation of a Jain image (verify); its Tirthankara identity is disputed (Sitalnath vs Padmaprabha). A museum compound now houses rescued sculptures; large parts of the three surviving temples are modern reconstructions. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Purulia' is the district HQ, not the actual village - the site is at Pakbirra village, Puncha block. COORDINATES APPROXIMATE: village-level geocode (23.15865, 86.68019), not an exact temple POI - verify on the ground.

name: Pakbirra Jain Temples
town: Pakbirra village, Puncha block (CSV town 'Purulia' is the district HQ, not the actual village)
town_description: Pakbirra (Pakbira) is a village in the Puncha block of Purulia district, West Bengal, about 40-50 km southeast of Purulia town on the Purulia-Puncha road. It is the largest archaeological spot in Purulia district, a former Jain religious complex with three surviving temples, scattered sculptures and a museum.
tradition: Jainism (Digambara vs Svetambara affiliation not stated in sources; the colossal naked Jina figure suggests Digambara - verify)
